clue.text: The musicians spotted by Conan Doyle

definitions.text: The musicians spotted by Conan Doyle

parts.words: The musicians spotted by Conan Doyle
parts.note: read literally, a group of players covered in spots; read as a title, a Sherlock Holmes story written by Arthur Conan Doyle

explanation.walkthrough: A spotted group of musicians is a speckled band, and that is also the title of a Sherlock Holmes adventure in which the 'band' is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sherlock Holmes short story is one of Arthur Conan Doyle's best known.

clue.text: Call it a day when these have passed

definitions.text: Call it a day when these have passed

parts.words: Call it a day when these have passed
parts.note: 'call it a day' usually means stop working, but literally a full day is complete once this span of time has gone by

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'call it a day' means stop, but here it is taken literally: a day really is over once the full span of hours has elapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole day, midnight to midnight, consists of this many hours.

clue.text: Ale is brewed for prophet

indicators.note: beer is brewed from mixed ingredients, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A beer is brewed in honour of a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Subdued pleasure trip resulting in sulking

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for playing quietly, a subdued sound
an outing is a pleasure trip

explanation.surface: A quiet day out ends with someone in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subdued' gives P, the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft; 'resulting in' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing out the lips is the typical expression of someone sulking.

clue.text: Comforted by shouted encouragement

explanation.surface: Someone is consoled by a crowd yelling support.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to raise their spirits, and also to urge them on with shouts of support.

clue.text: Robin Hood's county green

parts.note: Robin Hood's outlaws wore a cloth dyed green named after an English county town, which here seems to be a village green

explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln green was the cloth worn by Robin Hood's men; Lincoln is also a county town in eastern England, giving its name to Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is the traditional colour of Robin Hood's band.

clue.text: Advice to repudiate was void being out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled, so these words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recommendation to disown something because it was invalid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as an instruction: the answer, said as a command, is advice to repudiate.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown or deny something is to repudiate it; the imperative form is the advice itself.

clue.text: Nora often disguised after lunch

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters take on a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Nora often goes about in disguise once lunch is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day following the midday meal is the period between noon and evening.

clue.text: Tread a measure twice about two hours before midnight to curry favour

indicators.note: the doubled word goes around the time phrase, enclosing it
the word for treading a measure is written two times over

parts.note: to tread a measure is an old phrase for to dance
two hours before midnight is at ten o'clock

explanation.surface: Dancing a jig twice around ten at night to win someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles DANCE, and 'about' puts AT TEN between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance is to fuss over someone obsequiously, trying to win their goodwill.

clue.text: Sliced pie to cure an aesthetic pleasure-lover

indicators.note: a pie that is sliced is cut up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up a pie to cure a gourmet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Epicurean, after the philosopher Epicurus, devotes himself to refined pleasures, especially of food.

clue.text: Materially what a protesting occupier did?.

definitions.text: Materially what a protesting occupier did?

parts.words: Materially what a protesting occupier did
parts.note: 'Materially' points to a fabric, and a protester who occupies a building stages a sit-down there; the phrase for that in the past tense names the fabric

explanation.walkthrough: A protester who occupies premises 'sat in'; run together, the words name a glossy fabric, which is why the clue says 'Materially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy woven material.

clue.text: Comparatively disagreeable trial that is briefly right

parts.note: a test is a trial
i.e. is the short form of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A test that is, in short, rather unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: More irritable or tetchy is the comparative of a word meaning bad-tempered.

clue.text: Heads for the old boy poem

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: Pictures a former pupil penning verse about coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is the coin side bearing the head, not people or leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a coin bearing the monarch's portrait is the side called heads.

clue.text: The elder elver

parts.note: an elver is a young specimen of a certain fish, so the older form is the adult fish

explanation.walkthrough: Elvers are young fish; when they grow older they are adults of the same snakelike species.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvers are juvenile fish that mature into the adult snakelike swimmer.

clue.text: Sought fodder for late in life

parts.note: someone late in life is aged

explanation.surface: Someone looked for food for the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food, especially animal feed.

clue.text: Correctitude that goes with dexterity

explanation.definitionFit: It means correctness, and also the quality of being right-handed, which 'dexterity' literally means from Latin dexter, right.

clue.text: Here's the finish.

parts.note: the clue simply points to a word meaning the conclusion, as if marking it at the bottom of the page

explanation.walkthrough: A plain pointer to a word for the conclusion; it also supplies the 16 used in 28 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The conclusion of something is its close.

clue.text: Nautical poet just fitted for home security

parts.note: something just fitted is new
a bolt on a door is home security

explanation.surface: A sea poet has a fresh lock put on his door.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Newbolt wrote sea poems such as 'Drake's Drum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Newbolt is known for poems of the sea and the navy.

clue.text: … and the rest

parts.note: the phrase is the English for a Latin expression usually written in shortened form

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin et cetera means 'and the rest', usually written in its three-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera, abbreviated, means 'and other things'.

clue.text: Promote a rude GP improperly

indicators.note: done improperly, the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude doctor is wrongly given promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is a family doctor in Britain; here the letters are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to a higher grade is to promote them.

clue.text: Italian song with confused end guided an amazed Theseus

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in Italian opera

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so this word is scrambled

explanation.surface: An opera solo with a muddled finale helped a bewildered hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazed' means in the maze: in Greek myth Ariadne gave Theseus a thread to find his way out of the Labyrinth. 'confused' turns END into DNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne, daughter of King Minos, gave Theseus a thread to lead him out of the Labyrinth.

clue.text: Always Edward, as it turned out

parts.note: ever means always
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward, as it happened, was the same as ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Everted describes something turned inside out or outward.

clue.text: Formalised knowledge puts 101 in changed scene

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the rearranged word
changed letters are altered in order, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: 101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: A setting is altered by adding a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns SCENE into SENCE, and 'in' puts CI (101 in Roman numerals) inside after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Science is systematic, organised knowledge of the world.

clue.text: Begin the French scare

parts.note: start means begin
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: The French begin to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a sudden fright is to startle them.

clue.text: Examine creepy-crawly with quiet content

indicators.note: as content the quiet letter goes inside the bug word

parts.note: a creepy-crawly is an insect
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a bug that sits calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy', but it means contents: P is held inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look closely at something.

clue.text: Vessel which costs the trader money

explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank or container; VAT is also value added tax, a charge businesses must pay over.

clue.text: Oil then refined for emergency communications

indicators.note: refined oil is processed, so the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil is then refined for an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct phone link for urgent use.

clue.text: Alternative sea days tested for quality

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of these letters gives the answer

explanation.surface: Different days at sea are put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal is to test it for purity.

clue.text: Long 12 months before coming to the point

indicators.note: the year comes first, followed by the compass letter

parts.note: twelve months make a year
N (north) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A long year before reaching the main issue.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something.

clue.text: Rear higher before 16

indicators.note: the word for higher comes first, ahead of the cross-referenced word

parts.note: up means higher
16 refers to the answer of 16 Down, a word for finish

explanation.surface: Something rises higher before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' is a verb: to rear up or tip something over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend is to turn upright or on end, as a horse rears.

clue.text: Storehouse for the pastoral tenth

parts.note: farmers once owed a tenth of their produce to the parish clergy, kept in a special store building

explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of farm produce paid to support the church and its pastor; it was stored in a large barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithe barns held the tenth of crops given to the church.

clue.text: Postpone punishment and hang the words used

explanation.definitionFit: A court that delays a penalty suspends it; literally, to hang up a string of words is to suspend a sentence.
